claims.text: The route deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The GPS trace polyline between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event measures 18.0 km, and the platform's booked optimal route for the same endpoints is 10.0 km. The excess is 8.0 km and 80% of optimal, so both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), and the excess also crosses the materiality markers. Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is the trace figure; the rounded actual_distance_km copy on the trip_record is not citable for the threshold test and I do not cite it.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-09113; the trip started at 18:20:00, the first trace fix is 18:20:00, the last trace fix is 18:54:00 and the fare was charged at 18:54:03, and coverage is 100% with 205 fixes at 10 second intervals and no gaps. The artifacts therefore describe the same trip, and the excess in claim one is measured from an unimpaired trace.

No corroboration beyond the trace is required of this rider. POL-RD-08's final sentence imposes an extra corroboration requirement only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer; this rider's deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the condition does not arise and the trace alone carries the excess. I cite only these two named fields, which POL-GEN-01 permits for the POL-RD-08 test, and no other profile field.

The closure excuses only part of the excess, and the cap is arithmetic. The LTA advisory is a CLOSURE of the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector with a validity window (18:14 to 18:55) that overlaps the trip (18:20 to 18:54), and it records the shortest lawful alternative between the booked endpoints as 12.0 km. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(measured excess, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00), which is min(8.0, 3.60) = 3.60 km - the platform's own fare data records justified_excess_km of 3.60 and an adjusted optimal distance of 13.60 km. That leaves 4.40 km of excess unexoned. The driver's completed route was 18.0 km against a shortest lawful alternative of 12.0 km, i.e. 6.0 km more than the closure required, and 'there was a closure' cannot be stretched to cover that.

The driver cannot shift the unexonerated excess onto the rider as a rider-requested detour. The only chat traffic is the driver's own note that the closure is routing traffic around the industrial loop and the rider's reply 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion'. That reply is a message from the rider but it names no road or place, and its waypoint_hint is null, so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test (the vehicle passing within 200 m of the resolved waypoint) cannot be run on this record and cannot be supplied from general knowledge. In substance the rider authorised the lawful diversion - the 12.0 km signed alternative the advisory records - not an 18.0 km route; authorising a lawful diversion is not an instruction to drive further than that diversion requires.

The driver's counterparty statement that 'the closure forced a diversion' cites no evidence ID and no clause, and under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. It cannot extend the exoneration beyond what the advisory's own arithmetic supports, and the exoneration is capped by POL-RD-03 at 3.60 km of additional distance however the driver characterises the trip.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, and this is a METERED fare, so the clause applies. Running the computation against the closure-adjusted optimal route of 13.60 km and 27.2 minutes: (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0 surge multiplier on the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus the 1.00 of ERP lying on the optimal route, gives a recomputed fare of SGD 23.4160. The charged total was SGD 31.42, so the refund is SGD 8.004, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is SGD 8.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is only about 25.5% of the charged total, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not a full refund.

The SGD 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' ERP line is not added on top of that figure. It is flagged on_optimal_route false, and the POL-RD-02 recomputation above already excludes it from the recomputed fare, so it is comprehended in the SGD 8.05 and POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting it twice. I itemise it here for transparency only; the rider's total recovery on the distance and time lines remains SGD 8.05.

Separately from the distance refund, the SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' ERP line is a gantry the trace never passes. The nearest of the 205 recorded fixes comes 834 m from that gantry's coordinates, at 18:22:10, while the line was charged at 18:29:00 - far outside the 250 m radius POL-RD-09 treats as a crossing. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction available whether or not a deviation exists and recorded as a billing-integrity referral. It is not a line already refunded in the POL-RD-02 computation, because the recomputed fare published on the fare_breakdown retains that SGD 1.00 as an on-optimal-route charge.

POL-RD-03 is satisfied on its first two limbs. EV-ADVIS-09113-01 is a HIGH-severity CLOSURE of the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector - the very road the trip_record's own optimal-route snapshot traverses, which is recorded as 'routing-engine-v3.2 snapshot 2026-09-20 18:12 SGT via Pelton Canal Link, the segment named in the LTA advisory' - and the advisory carries intersects_route true. Its validity window of 18:14 to 18:55 on 2026-09-20 overlaps the trip window of 18:20 to 18:54, with 34.0 minutes of overlap recorded, so the advisory covers the trip.

The third limb of POL-RD-03 is also met: the actual route left the optimal corridor before the closed segment and rejoined it after. EV-GPS-09113 runs 18.0 km over 205 fixes from 18:20:00 to 18:54:00, and the Industrial loop exit gantry that EV-FARE-09113 records as NOT on the optimal route was crossed at 18:31:50, 223.17 m from trace fix 71 - placing the vehicle on the signed industrial diversion rather than on the closed Pelton Canal Link connector. That is a closure-forced diversion, not a driver's shortcut.

The exoneration is capped, and the cap bites hard. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(measured excess 8.0 km, 1.30 x (shortest lawful alternative 12.0 km - booked optimal 10.0 km) + 1.00) = 3.60 km, so only 3.60 km of the 8.0 km excess is excused by the closure. The closure-adjusted optimal is therefore 13.60 km, and its duration is the booked 20.0 minutes scaled by 13.60/10.00 = 27.2 minutes; trip_record.amended_optimal_duration_min is null, so no stored figure displaces that scaling.

After the POL-RD-03 adjustment the excess remaining is 4.4 km on an adjusted optimal of 13.60 km - about 32% - which passes the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km) but fails BOTH material thresholds (50% of optimal, and 8.0 km absolute). The derived status 'material' on EV-GPS-09113 was computed on the pre-adjustment excess of 8.0 km, and POL-RD-01 expressly requires materiality to be assessed on the excess REMAINING after any POL-RD-03 adjustment, not on the excess as first measured. This is therefore a non-material deviation, and POL-RD-06's profile check, its FULL_REFUND uplift and its driver-conduct referral are all unavailable on this trip.

The refund must be run against the closure-adjusted baseline, and it lands at SGD 8.05 and no more. POL-RD-02 gives recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x surge_multiplier 1.0 (read from EV-FARE-09113, which is the only artifact carrying that field) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP for the one gantry lying on the optimal route = 23.416, so the refund is 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded UP to SGD 8.05. The 12.75 figure carried in EV-FARE-09113's other refund block is computed against the unadjusted 10.0 km optimal of a closure-blind computation and is superseded once POL-RD-03 applies.

The 2.80 charged at the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is off-route ERP and is already comprehended inside that 8.004 refund: the recomputed fare of 23.416 carries only the 1.00 Pelton gantry that lies on the optimal route, which is precisely why the refund is 8.004 rather than 5.204. Under POL-RD-09(1) off-route ERP must NEVER be added on top of a POL-RD-02 figure, so any claim for 8.05 plus 2.80, or for the whole 3.80 of ERP, is the double count that limb exists to prevent.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be established on the only fields POL-RD-06 permits it to consult: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610, a ratio of 0.00 - far below the 3-flag test and far below the 0.05 ratio with at least 40 completed trips. POL-GEN-01 confines this test to those two fields and makes every other counter on the driver profile context only, so no uplift of the remedy and no conduct referral arises from this driver's record.

The driver's exoneration rests on an unimpaired trace, not on a data failure. EV-GPS-09113 carries 205 fixes at a 10 second sample interval over 100% coverage, with an empty gaps list and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) is engaged and the trace needs no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii). The POL-RD-03 finding therefore stands on clean evidence, and there is no data gap on which to escalate.

On POL-RD-04, the rider did not merely fail to object: at 18:22:40 the driver reported that the Pelton Canal Link closure was sending traffic around the industrial loop, and at 18:23:10 the rider replied 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion.' That is a rider-sourced instruction given within three minutes of the diversion starting, referring to the specific diversion route the driver had just identified, and the trace corroborates it by running that diversion and crossing the Industrial loop exit gantry at 18:31:50. To the extent the excess is attributable to that instruction, POL-RD-04 excludes the distance driven between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied.

Driver, your POL-RD-04 argument that the rider asked for the detour does not run. Refund under POL-RD-02 (METERED fare): recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0 surge (read from EV-FARE-09113) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP lying on the optimal route = 23.416. Charged total 31.42. Refund = 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05 - about 25% of the charge, so a partial refund, not a full one.

ERP. The 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' line is off-route ERP and is ALREADY COMPREHENDED in the 8.05, because the recomputed fare carries only the on-optimal-route gantry; it is itemised for transparency and never added on top (POL-RD-09(1)). Total refund: 8.05 + 1.00 = SGD 9.05. No driver compensation is due: the fare billed the full 18.0 km, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall, and no repeat-deviation pattern exists. Profiles were used only for the tests POL-GEN-01 permits. Confidence 0.9 - every artifact carrying a deciding fact is at full weight.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' ERP line is a charge for a gantry the GPS trace never passes (nearest of 205 fixes 834 m away, outside the 250 m match radius) and has been refunded as a standalone correction; refer the line for billing-integrity review.

The GPS trace polyline between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event measures 18.0 km, and the platform's booked optimal route for the same endpoints is 10.0 km. The excess is 8.0 km and 80% of optimal, so both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), and the excess also crosses the materiality markers. Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is the trace figure; the rounded actual_distance_km copy on the trip_record is not citable for the threshold test and I do not cite it.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The artifacts therefore describe the same trip, and the excess in claim one is measured from an unimpaired trace.

No corroboration beyond the trace is required of this rider. POL-RD-08's final sentence imposes an extra corroboration requirement only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer; this rider's deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the condition does not arise and the trace alone carries the excess. I cite only these two named fields, which POL-GEN-01 permits for the POL-RD-08 test, and no other profile field.

The closure excuses only part of the excess, and the cap is arithmetic. The LTA advisory is a CLOSURE of the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector with a validity window (18:14 to 18:55) that overlaps the trip (18:20 to 18:54), and it records the shortest lawful alternative between the booked endpoints as 12.0 km. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(measured excess, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00), which is min(8.0, 3.60) = 3.60 km - the platform's own fare data records justified_excess_km of 3.60 and an adjusted optimal distance of 13.60 km. That leaves 4.40 km of excess unexoned. The driver's completed route was 18.0 km against a shortest lawful alternative of 12.0 km, i.e. 6.0 km more than the closure required, and 'there was a closure' cannot be stretched to cover that.

The driver cannot shift the unexonerated excess onto the rider as a rider-requested detour. The only chat traffic is the driver's own note that the closure is routing traffic around the industrial loop and the rider's reply 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion'. That reply is a message from the rider but it names no road or place, and its waypoint_hint is null, so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test (the vehicle passing within 200 m of the resolved waypoint) cannot be run on this record and cannot be supplied from general knowledge. In substance the rider authorised the lawful diversion - the 12.0 km signed alternative the advisory records - not an 18.0 km route; authorising a lawful diversion is not an instruction to drive further than that diversion requires.

The driver's counterparty statement that 'the closure forced a diversion' cites no evidence ID and no clause, and under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. It cannot extend the exoneration beyond what the advisory's own arithmetic supports, and the exoneration is capped by POL-RD-03 at 3.60 km of additional distance however the driver characterises the trip.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, and this is a METERED fare, so the clause applies. Running the computation against the closure-adjusted optimal route of 13.60 km and 27.2 minutes: (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0 surge multiplier on the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus the 1.00 of ERP lying on the optimal route, gives a recomputed fare of SGD 23.4160. The charged total was SGD 31.42, so the refund is SGD 8.004, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is SGD 8.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is only about 25.5% of the charged total, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not a full refund.

The SGD 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' ERP line is not added on top of that figure. It is flagged on_optimal_route false, and the POL-RD-02 recomputation above already excludes it from the recomputed fare, so it is comprehended in the SGD 8.05 and POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting it twice. I itemise it here for transparency only; the rider's total recovery on the distance and time lines remains SGD 8.05.

Separately from the distance refund, the SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' ERP line is a gantry the trace never passes. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction available whether or not a deviation exists and recorded as a billing-integrity referral.
